summary: Opengist is a self-hosted pastebin application that stores snippets using Git as the underlying mechanism. It provides a web interface for managing text snippets and code sharing within your own infrastructure. The project is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 and is actively maintained.
goodFor: It suits teams or individuals who want a private, Git-backed alternative to public pastebins for sharing code snippets.
watchOut: The AGPL-3.0 licence places strong copyleft requirements on your deployment if you modify and network the software. It also introduces the operational overhead of managing Git repositories compared to standard database-backed pastebins.
deployNotes: As it relies on Docker, Go, and Node.js, you will typically need to configure persistent volumes for your Git data and set up a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
